title: MSI XpertStation WS300 Review NVIDIA DGX Station GB300
gist: ServeTheHome reviews MSI's XpertStation WS300, its second NVIDIA DGX Station (GB300) system. It is a $100K+ deskside tower with a 72-core Grace CPU, a Blackwell Ultra GPU with 252GB HBM3E, dual 400G ConnectX-8 ports, a 1.6kW PSU that effectively needs a dedicated 20A circuit, and a weight of nearly 30kg. The captured text covers only specs and the exterior and I/O tour; it ends before the internal hardware and performance sections.

themes.theme: Server-grade AI hardware on the desktop

insights.claim: NVIDIA GB300-based DGX Station systems such as MSI's XpertStation WS300 bring server-grade NVIDIA hardware to a deskside computer for the first time, so developers can test and run AI workloads locally.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: This opens a new high-ASP workstation market for NVIDIA and its OEM partners (MSI, Gigabyte).
insights.quote: These NVIDIA GB300-based systems bring NVIDIA’s server-grade hardware to a desk-side computer for the first time

insights.claim: The MSI XpertStation WS300 pairs an NVIDIA Grace 72-core Neoverse V2 CPU with 496GB of LPDDR5X (396GB/s) and a Blackwell Ultra GPU with 252GB of HBM3E (7.1TB/s). Storage is two PCIe Gen6 x4 and two Gen5 x4 M.2 slots.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: HBM3E content in desktop systems adds incremental HBM demand.

insights.claim: The WS300 is described as a $100K+ system in an understated black tower measuring about 53cm tall and 57cm deep and weighing nearly 30kg.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: A price above $100K puts DGX Station in enterprise capex budgets rather than prosumer spending, which limits volume but carries high revenue per unit.
insights.quote: you would be hard-pressed to guess it is a $100K+ system with a server processor set tucked inside
insights.locator: The WS300’s overall design is typical

insights.claim: DGX Station systems use a standardized NVIDIA motherboard, so all Station systems share the same rear I/O. Vendors such as MSI differentiate on chassis, cooling and accommodating an RTX PRO graphics card.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: NVIDIA captures most of the platform value, while OEMs compete on thin mechanical and thermal differentiation.

insights.claim: ServeTheHome networked two DGX Station systems using the NVIDIA ConnectX-8 SuperNIC for an 800Gbps aggregate Blackwell Ultra-to-Blackwell Ultra RDMA link. Unlike earlier workstations, where networking was an afterthought, MSI and NVIDIA make it central to scaling to more users and larger models.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: NVIDIA networking attaches even to workstation sales, which extends its networking revenue beyond the data centre.
insights.quote: Unlike many pre-AI-era workstations where networking was an afterthought, here MSI and NVIDIA are making it central to scaling

insights.claim: The WS300's Marvell 10GbE controller connects through the ConnectX-8 SuperNIC's built-in PCIe switch rather than directly to the CPU. The system has no USB4 ports, so transfers above 10Gbps must go through the dual 400Gb QSFP112 ports.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: ConnectX-8 doubles as the platform's I/O hub, which deepens NVIDIA's silicon content per system.
insights.quote: MSI’s Marvell 10Gbase-T controller is attached to the NVIDIA ConnectX-8 SuperNIC’s built-in PCIe switch, then to the CPU.

insights.claim: ServeTheHome's view is that the DGX Station is better used as a server connected over the network than as a traditional workstation with added peripherals.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: DGX Station competes more with small on-premises servers than with high-end PCs.
insights.quote: we think it is better used as a server you connect to over the network

insights.claim: DGX Station systems sit at the limit of a single North American outlet with a 1600W 80 PLUS Platinum PSU. They need a C19 power cable and a 20-amp circuit, and in practice effectively require a dedicated 20A circuit.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Office electrical limits cap deskside AI compute density, so larger deployments are pushed back to data centres or require facility upgrades.
insights.quote: In practice, this system effectively requires its own dedicated 20A circuit.

insights.claim: Because Blackwell Ultra is a compute accelerator with no true integrated display GPU, the BMC provides the only out-of-the-box graphics output, and full graphics requires pairing with a compatible NVIDIA RTX PRO Blackwell card.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: An RTX PRO card is an upsell attached to each DGX Station, adding NVIDIA revenue.

insights.claim: Compared with Gigabyte's DGX Station system, MSI keeps the front of the WS300 open for airflow, moving all ports and buttons to the top, and gives the QSFP112 cages better passive cooling.
insights.speaker: Ryan Smith
insights.so_what: Thermal design is the main differentiator among DGX Station OEMs.
